steps.name: Surfaces
steps.narration: Every NOVA screen starts from the same dark navy surfaces. These are tokens: named values, set in one place.
steps.prompt: Find the canvas colour. Why is the maths drawn on a darker panel than the page?

steps.name: Fonts
steps.narration: Inter is for words and buttons. Cambria Math is for maths, so x, fractions and powers always look like maths.
steps.prompt: Which font would you use for 3x + 5? Which for a button label?

steps.name: Colour language
steps.narration: Seven maths roles, seven colours. Blue is given, gold is unknown, cyan is an operation, green is the result.
steps.prompt: Say the role for each colour before you read its label.

steps.name: Shapes too
steps.narration: Colour is never the only clue. Each role also has a shape: square, dashed circle, diamond, tick, cross, star, triangle.
steps.prompt: Cover the colours. Can you still tell the roles apart by shape?

steps.name: Read an equation
steps.narration: Here is 3x + 5 = 20. Given numbers are blue squares, x is the gold unknown, and the signs are cyan operations.
steps.prompt: Which part is the unknown? How do you know without the colour?

steps.name: Colour-blind check
steps.narration: This is the same equation for someone who sees no colour. The shapes and outlines still carry the meaning.
steps.prompt: Is anything now impossible to tell apart? That would be a design bug.

steps.name: Solved
steps.narration: When we solve it, the answer turns green with a tick: x = 5. Same language, in every lesson.
steps.prompt: Which role changed when the equation was solved?

steps.name: Grid
steps.narration: Everything starts on a grid. It keeps lines straight and spacing equal.
steps.prompt: Why does equal spacing matter on a number line?

steps.name: Axes
steps.narration: The number line is an axis: ticks at equal steps, with an arrow showing it carries on.
steps.prompt: What is the interval between ticks here?

steps.name: Arrows
steps.narration: An arrow hops from the start. Cyan for adding, orange for subtracting, so the direction is clear.
steps.prompt: Which way would a negative hop go?

steps.name: Braces
steps.narration: A brace groups a length and names it. It counts the jumps, not the ticks.
steps.prompt: How many jumps does the brace cover?

steps.name: Arcs
steps.narration: An arc marks an angle at a vertex. At exactly 90 degrees it becomes a square box.
steps.prompt: Is this angle acute, right or obtuse?

steps.name: Labels
steps.narration: Labels name points in italics. The dashes show equal sides and the dimension line gives a length.
steps.prompt: Which two sides are marked equal?

steps.name: Together
steps.narration: Grid, axes, arrows, braces, arcs and labels. Every NOVA diagram is built from these six pieces.
steps.prompt: Name one lesson that would use each primitive.

steps.name: Start
steps.narration: The helper starts at 0. Nothing has happened yet: that is step zero, not a jump.
steps.prompt: Where does the helper start? Is that a jump?

steps.name: Jump 1
steps.narration: Jump 1: 4 to 4. Total moved so far: 1 × 4 = 4.
steps.prompt: Before you step: where will jump 1 land?

steps.name: Jump 2
steps.narration: Jump 2: 4 to 8. Total moved so far: 2 × 4 = 8.
steps.prompt: Before you step: where will jump 2 land?

steps.name: Jump 3
steps.narration: Jump 3: 4 to 12. Total moved so far: 3 × 4 = 12.
steps.prompt: Before you step: where will jump 3 land?

steps.name: Total
steps.narration: 3 jumps of 4 from 0 lands on 12. Count jumps, not tick marks.

steps.name: Drag-snap
steps.narration: Drag the marker and let go: it snaps to the nearest 0.25. Dropped at 1.3, it snaps to 1.25. Arrow keys move it one step.
steps.prompt: Dropped at 1.3 with steps of 0.25: where does it snap?

steps.name: Slider
steps.narration: The slider sets the same value. Slide to 1.5 and the marker follows. One value, many controls.
steps.prompt: If the slider reads 1.5, where is the marker?

steps.name: Stepper
steps.narration: The stepper adds or takes one step. 1.5 plus one step of 0.25 is 1.75.
steps.prompt: What is 1.5 plus one step of 0.25?

steps.name: Entry
steps.narration: Type an answer as a fraction, decimal or percent. 3/4, 0.75 and 75% all land on the same point.

steps.name: Sort
steps.narration: Sort by value, not by how the numbers look. −0.5 is smallest; 0.3 is less than 1/3 because 1/3 is 0.333…

steps.name: Match
steps.narration: Match each fraction to its decimal. 3/5 is 0.6, not 0.35: the digits are a trap.

steps.name: All linked
steps.narration: Every control reads and writes the same value and emits a value event. Engines just choose which ones to show.
steps.prompt: Which control would you use on a phone?

steps.name: Fractions
steps.narration: A fraction is stacked: numerator over a bar over denominator. Three quarters plus one quarter is one whole.
steps.prompt: Read it aloud: what is on top, what is underneath?
steps.note: Not 3/4 + 1/4 = 4/8: add the tops, keep the bottom.

steps.name: Mixed numbers
steps.narration: Two and one third: the whole number sits beside the fraction. As an improper fraction it is seven thirds.
steps.prompt: How many thirds are in 2 wholes?

steps.name: Powers
steps.narration: The small raised 3 is a power: 2 cubed means three 2s multiplied, which is 8.
steps.prompt: Is 2 cubed the same as 2 times 3?

steps.name: Roots
steps.narration: The root sign has a bar over everything inside it. The square root of 49 is 7; the cube root of 27 is 3.

steps.name: Surds
steps.narration: A surd is a root left exact. Root 12 is root 4 times root 3, and root 4 is 2, so it simplifies to 2 root 3.
steps.note: √12 is not 6: halving is not square rooting.

steps.name: Standard form
steps.narration: Standard form is a number from 1 up to 10, times a power of ten. 32 000 is 3.2 times 10 to the power 4.
steps.prompt: How many places does the point move?
steps.note: 32 × 10³ is not standard form: 32 is not less than 10.

steps.name: All together
steps.narration: One markup for every engine: it looks right, and a screen reader says it right.
steps.prompt: Which one would you read aloud as “x to the power 6”?

steps.name: Seed
steps.narration: A seed is a starting code. From it the randomiser makes a stream of numbers that looks random but is fixed by the seed.
steps.prompt: If you use the same seed again, what happens?

steps.name: Same seed
steps.narration: Same seed, same questions. MATHS7 gives exactly the same six questions on every device, so a class can share one worksheet.
steps.prompt: Are the two sets the same?

steps.name: New seed
steps.narration: Change the seed and you get a fresh set. Dashed cards changed; that is a new variant of the same skill.
steps.prompt: What changed, and what stayed the same?

steps.name: Constraints
steps.narration: Rules keep variants fair: no repeats, no times 0 or times 1, and whole-number answers. Random does not mean anything goes.

steps.name: Templates
steps.narration: The same seed drives any template: equations, fractions, percentages or standard form. The skill changes; the seed still recreates it.
steps.prompt: Pick a template you would use for homework.

steps.name: Fork per question
steps.narration: Each question has its own stream. Re-roll Q3 and Q1, Q2 and the rest stay put, so a teacher can swap one question without changing the others.

steps.name: All set
steps.narration: Seed, template and rules: that is all an engine needs to make endless fair variants it can always recreate.
steps.prompt: Write down the seed so you can get this set back.

steps.name: State
steps.narration: Each engine keeps a small state: here, a bar of 4 parts with none shaded. The state is the single source of truth.
steps.prompt: What fraction is shaded right now?

steps.name: value
steps.narration: Every change fires a value event: which key, the new value and where it came from. Shade 3 parts, three value events.
steps.prompt: How many value events for 3 clicks?

steps.name: step
steps.narration: Moving through a lesson fires a step event with the step number and its name.
steps.prompt: What would the next step event say?

steps.name: correct
steps.narration: Checking fires a correct event: true or false, plus what was checked. 3 of 4 parts is three quarters, so correct is true.

steps.name: hintUsed
steps.narration: Asking for help fires hintUsed with a count. Hints are information, not penalties.
steps.prompt: Which event tells a teacher a hint was used?

steps.name: Undo / redo
steps.narration: Undo and redo restore earlier states and announce it with value events marked undo or redo.

steps.name: Listeners
steps.narration: Other parts listen without knowing the engine: a report counts attempts, correct answers and hints. No scores here; games live in F0-12.

steps.name: All signals
steps.narration: value, correct, step and hintUsed: four signals every engine speaks, so any lesson, game or report can plug in.

steps.name: Script
steps.narration: Every step gets a script line with slots in curly brackets, like n, lo and hi. One script works for any number.
steps.prompt: Which slots does this line need?

steps.name: Fill slots
steps.narration: The engine fills the slots with live values: 47 sits between 40 and 50. Change the number and the words change too.
steps.prompt: What goes in the lo slot for 47?

steps.name: Halfway
steps.narration: The next line names the halfway point, 45, the deciding line for rounding.

steps.name: Tone
steps.narration: Same maths, brisker tone. Each line can come in a warm or a brisk version, so lessons can pick the voice that fits.
steps.prompt: Is the brisk line saying anything different?

steps.name: Length
steps.narration: Short versions keep the key fact for small screens or quick recaps. 47 is above 45.
steps.prompt: What did the short line keep?

steps.name: Transcript
steps.narration: Each line said goes into a transcript, so pupils can scroll back and screen readers can catch up. 47 rounds to 50.

steps.name: Hooks
steps.narration: Other parts can listen to the narration hook: captions, a voice, or a teacher log. Bob speaks once, everyone hears.
steps.prompt: Name one thing that could listen to Bob.

steps.name: Registry
steps.narration: Every engine registers itself: an id, a title, what kind it is, its topics and what it depends on. Seventeen foundation parts so far.

steps.name: Lookup
steps.narration: Lessons can look parts up by topic. Ask for "number" and you get the maths text renderer and the worked example stepper.

steps.name: Manifest
steps.narration: A lesson manifest is a list of steps. Each step names a component, a mode and a learning objective: here, fractions of amounts.

steps.name: Validate
steps.narration: Validation catches mistakes before pupils see them: F0-99 is not a real component, and "play" is not a mode.

steps.name: Fix
steps.narration: Point step 4 at F0-11 and use challenge mode. Now the manifest is valid.

steps.name: Load order
steps.narration: The registry works out the load order: shared parts like design tokens and events come before the engines that need them.

steps.name: Objectives
steps.narration: Each objective links to its steps, so a report can say how pupils did on O1 and O2 separately.

steps.name: Shell
steps.narration: The gallery shell is the frame every bank page sits in: a header, filters, a search box and a grid of engine tiles.
steps.prompt: What three parts does the shell have?

steps.name: From the registry
steps.narration: Tiles come straight from the registry, so a new engine appears in the gallery as soon as it registers. No hand-made lists.
steps.prompt: Where does the tile list come from?

steps.name: Filter
steps.narration: Topic chips filter the grid. Choose geometry and only the SVG primitives and the geometry canvas stay.
steps.prompt: How many geometry tools are there?

steps.name: Search
steps.narration: Search matches ids and titles: type "plot" and you get the axes and plotting primitive, F0-14.

steps.name: Topic layer
steps.narration: Switch the style layer to algebra and the accents turn gold. Same shell, different topic mood, no extra code.

steps.name: Status
steps.narration: Badges show what is built (tick) and what is planned (dotted circle): shape as well as colour, so it works for everyone.

steps.name: Print
steps.narration: For print the shell drops its glow and turns into a clean light catalogue a teacher can hand out.

steps.name: Question types
steps.narration: One engine, four question types: numeric, multiple choice, select-all and put-in-order. Every question carries its marks and objective.

steps.name: Mark
steps.narration: A quarter of 24 is 6. The marker compares the answer and awards the mark.

steps.name: Equivalent answers
steps.narration: 3/4, 0.75 and .75 are the same number, so all of them score. Pupils are not punished for a different form.

steps.name: Method marks
steps.narration: Three quarters of 24 is worth 2 marks. This pupil found 24 ÷ 4 = 6 but slipped: 6 × 3 is 18, not 16. M1 for the method, no A1.
steps.prompt: Why does the pupil get 1 mark?

steps.name: Misconceptions
steps.narration: An answer of 6 for three quarters is a known trap: it is only one quarter. The feedback names the slip, not just "wrong".

steps.name: By objective
steps.narration: Results group by objective. O1 is strong; O2, non-unit fractions, needs more work. The striped bar marks the gap.

steps.name: Report
steps.narration: Marks, method credit, misconception notes and objective scores: everything a teacher needs, with no scores turned into games here.

steps.narration: A quarter of 24 is 6. The marker compares the answer and awards the mark.

steps.name: Equivalent answers
steps.narration: 3/4, 0.75 and .75 are the same number, so all of them score. Pupils are not punished for a different form.

steps.name: Method marks
steps.narration: Three quarters of 24 is worth 2 marks. This pupil found 24 ÷ 4 = 6 but slipped: 6 × 3 is 18, not 16. M1 for the method, no A1.
steps.prompt: Why does the pupil get 1 mark?

steps.name: Misconceptions
steps.narration: An answer of 6 for three quarters is a known trap: it is only one quarter. The feedback names the slip, not just "wrong".

steps.name: By objective
steps.narration: Results group by objective. O1 is strong; O2, non-unit fractions, needs more work. The striped bar marks the gap.

steps.name: Report
steps.narration: Marks, method credit, misconception notes and objective scores: everything a teacher needs, with no scores turned into games here.

traps.20: That subtracts 4. A quarter means share into 4 equal parts.
traps.96: That is 24 × 4. A quarter means divide by 4.

steps.name: Wrap
steps.narration: The game wrapper sits around any engine. Engines just say right or wrong; the wrapper adds rounds, score, lives and hints.
steps.prompt: Who keeps the score: the engine or the wrapper?

steps.name: Score
steps.narration: 3/4 of 24 is 18. Correct: plus 10 points.
steps.prompt: How many points for a correct answer?

steps.name: Streak
steps.narration: 2/5 of 30 is 12. Two in a row starts a streak, worth a 5 point bonus.

steps.name: Lives
steps.narration: 1/3 of 27 is 9, not 8. No points, the streak resets and one life is lost.

steps.name: Hints
steps.narration: A hint costs 5 points. Helpful, never free, never a punishment that ends the game.

steps.name: Reactions
steps.narration: 5/8 of 40 is 25. Bob and the helper react to every answer, with poses that change for right and wrong.
steps.prompt: Which pose shows for a right answer?

steps.name: Results
steps.narration: At the end: score, percentage, stars and best streak. Four out of five is 80 percent: two stars.

steps.name: I do: set up
steps.narration: I do: I solve one while you watch. First, write the equation: 3x + 5 = 20.

steps.name: I do: undo +5
steps.narration: Subtract 5 from both sides to undo the plus 5. That leaves 3x = 15. Each line has its reason beside it.

steps.name: I do: undo ×3
steps.narration: Divide both sides by 3: x = 5. Then check by substituting back. 3 times 5 plus 5 is 20.

steps.name: We do: blanks
steps.narration: We do: a similar one together. 4x − 3 = 17. Add 3 to both sides. What goes in the blank?

steps.name: We do: fade
steps.narration: 4x = 20. Now the reasons start to fade: you supply the why. Divide by 4 to get x.

steps.name: You do
steps.narration: You do: 2x + 7 = 19 on your own. No reasons, no blanks filled. Same steps as before.

steps.name: Check
steps.narration: Subtract 7, then divide by 2: x = 6. I do, we do, you do: support fades as confidence grows.

steps.name: Axes
steps.narration: Every chart starts with axes and a scale. x goes across from −1 to 5; y goes up in steps of 2.

steps.name: Plot points
steps.narration: For y = 2x + 1: when x is 0, y is 1; x is 1, y is 3; x is 2, y is 5. Coordinates are (across, up).

steps.name: Line
steps.narration: The points line up, so join them with a straight line: y = 2x + 1.

steps.name: Gradient and intercept
steps.narration: Up 2 for every 1 across: the gradient is 2. The line crosses the y axis at 1: the intercept.

steps.name: Scatter
steps.narration: Scatter graphs show pairs of data. Taller pupils tend to have longer arm spans: positive correlation.

steps.name: Bars
steps.narration: Bar charts compare categories on one scale. Grape is the most popular, with 9 votes. Patterns tell the bars apart without colour.

steps.name: Read a value
steps.narration: To read a value, go up from x = 3 to the line, then across: y = 7.

steps.name: Table
steps.narration: A table of values lists x values and works out y for each. Here the rule is y = 3x − 2.
steps.prompt: What rule fills the y row?

steps.name: Fill
steps.narration: Substitute each x. When x is −1: 3 times −1 is −3, take 2 is −5.

steps.name: Differences
steps.narration: Look along the row: y goes up by 3 each time x goes up by 1. That constant difference is the gradient.

steps.name: Link to graph
steps.narration: Each column is a coordinate. Plot them and they line up on y = 3x − 2.

steps.name: Highlight
steps.narration: Highlight a column and its point lights up too: x = 2, y = 4 is the point (2, 4).

steps.name: Spot the error
steps.narration: If a value is wrong, the point jumps off the line. 5 should be 4: 3 times 2 is 6, take 2 is 4.

steps.name: Complete
steps.narration: Complete table, steady differences, points on a line: the table and the graph tell the same story.

steps.name: Snap grid
steps.narration: Points snap to the grid, so coordinates stay exact. A is at (1, 1), B at (8, 1), C at (3, 6).

steps.name: Lines
steps.narration: Join the points with line segments to make triangle ABC.

steps.name: Measure
steps.narration: The canvas measures each side. AB runs along the grid: 7 units. The slanted sides use Pythagoras behind the scenes.

steps.name: Angles
steps.narration: Each angle is measured at its vertex and marked with an arc.

steps.name: Angle sum
steps.narration: Add the three angles: always 180 degrees, whatever the triangle.
steps.prompt: What do the angles add to?

steps.name: Right angle
steps.narration: A right angle gets a square mark, not an arc. This is a 3, 4, 5 triangle.

steps.name: Straight line
steps.narration: Angles on a straight line also add to 180 degrees. Drag the points in Explore to test it.
steps.prompt: What do angles on a line add to?

steps.name: Why static
steps.narration: Animations are great on screen, but paper and old devices need a still version. Every engine keeps a static fallback.
steps.prompt: When would you need a static version?

steps.name: Snapshot
steps.narration: The renderer copies the live SVG, fixes its colours inline and turns it into a PNG image, with the same alt text.
steps.prompt: What file type is the snapshot?

steps.name: Print theme
steps.narration: Print swaps the dark glowing theme for white paper and black ink. Easier to read, kinder to the printer.
steps.prompt: Why switch to a light theme?

steps.name: Worksheet
steps.narration: A worksheet has a title, a name line, the seed and questions in two columns with space to answer.
steps.prompt: How many questions on this sheet?

steps.name: Seeds
steps.narration: Change the seed and you get a fresh sheet; keep it and you get the same questions every time, so a class can share one.
steps.prompt: What gives the same sheet again?

steps.name: Answer key
steps.narration: The answer key prints on its own page. 3/4 of 24 style questions, answers ready to mark.

steps.name: Export
steps.narration: Print it straight away or download a standalone sheet. No internet needed once it is saved.
